source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 21 April 1927, p. 10 ("Mr. Newell has walk-over")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: image-read (BNA article image, art 179): 'Mr. Joseph Newell, J.P., was returned unopposed for the Dungannon division of the Tyrone County Council.'

note: Triennial election, polled 1 June 1927; nominations Wednesday 20 April 1927. Dungannon is absent from the Derry Journal's list because, as in 1924, the urban divisions were nominated locally; the Belfast Telegraph of 21 April 1927, p. 10, reports that Mr. Joseph Newell, J.P., was returned unopposed for the Dungannon division. That makes 27 divisions (the 1930 total). Returned unopposed. The Belfast News-Letter of 15 April 1927, p. 9 (OCR, finding aid only) reports a meeting in Dungannon that again selected Mr. Joseph Newell, J.P., the outgoing member. He sat for Dungannon from 1924 (Mid-Ulster Mail, 19 April 1924, p. 5); J. M. Williamson holds it in 1930.
